title: U.S. Treasury Yield Curve
revision_note: FRED's H.15 constant-maturity series are not revised after publication.
methodology: Daily par yields for all eleven standard Treasury constant-maturity tenors (1mo, 3mo, 6mo, 1yr, 2yr, 3yr, 5yr, 7yr, 10yr, 20yr, 30yr), each its own FRED H.15 series (DGS1MO–DGS30), joined on date.

The full published history is fetched, not a trailing window: DGS1, DGS3, DGS5, DGS10 and DGS20 begin 1962-01-02, and the remaining tenors phase in as Treasury began issuing them — DGS30 in 1977-02, DGS7 in 1969-07, DGS2 in 1976-06, DGS3MO/DGS6MO in 1981-09, and DGS1MO in 2001-07. A date carries only the tenors that actually reported, so an early-1960s snapshot is a five-point curve and the full eleven-point curve exists only from 2001-07.
notes: This page draws the curve as a snapshot: one date's yields across every tenor, on a categorical, evenly spaced axis (Bloomberg convention) rather than a calendar-spaced one. The same data plotted the other way — one tenor across every date — is “Treasury Yields by Tenor”, which reads this same file.

The 20-year tenor (DGS20) has a gap from 1987-01 to 1993-09 — its last value before it is 1986-12-31 and its next is 1993-10-01 — while Treasury was not issuing 20-year bonds. The chart leaves the gap visible rather than interpolating across it. **Corrected 2026-09-17**: this note previously gave the gap as 2002-02-18 to 2006-02-08, which is neither the right tenor nor the right dates — those are the 30-year bond's suspension. The error was invisible while a 6300-row fetch cap held this series' history back to roughly 2002, since the real gap falls entirely outside that window; widening the fetch to FRED's full 1962 history exposed it. Checked against a fresh FRED pull: DGS30 reports continuously across 2002-2006 and has no gap at all, and DGS20 reports continuously across it too.
Values are percent, not a decimal fraction.

Fetched with no row limit as of 2026-09-17. Before that the fetcher capped the request at 6300 rows sorted newest-first, which silently truncated the history to roughly 2002 — the apparent start date was an artifact of the cap, not a choice, and would have begun dropping observations off the left edge as the series grew.
